result.secondOpinionBoundary: A disagreement usually means this person sits close to a cut-off. It is not a fault, but it is a good reason for the doctor to look sooner.
result.attributionHint: Each reading is compared with a typical person in the training data. This shows what moved the neural model's score. It is not medical advice.

result.attributionNoEffect: Made no difference to the score:
result.attributionCaveat: These comparisons come from the training cohort, not from Indian reference ranges. A reading can be clinically high and still sit below this dataset's average — the reasons list above uses Indian cut-offs, and that is what the referral is based on.

modelCard.title: About the risk model
modelCard.intro: This screen exists so nobody has to take the risk score on trust. Everything the model is built on is listed here.
modelCard.algorithmBody: A decision tree, limited to four questions deep on purpose. Every result can be read back as a short chain of comparisons, which is why the app can tell a health worker why a patient was flagged instead of only showing a number.
modelCard.metricsHint: Measured on held-out data the model never saw during training.
modelCard.recallNote: The model is deliberately tuned to catch cases rather than to avoid false alarms. For screening, sending a healthy person for a confirmatory test is a much smaller harm than missing a diabetic one.
modelCard.referencesTitle: Reference ranges used in the explanations
modelCard.notDiagnosis: This tool screens. It does not diagnose. Only a laboratory test and a doctor can do that.
modelCard.loadError: Could not load the model details. They are also in the project's ml/README.md.
modelCard.secondOpinionHint: A small neural network, trained on the same data
modelCard.secondOpinionNotPrimary: This model does not set the risk band. The decision tree does.
modelCard.secondOpinionBody: It runs alongside the tree for two reasons. It can say how much each of the eight readings contributed, which a four-question tree cannot. And when the two models place someone in different bands, that person is near a cut-off and worth seeing sooner.
modelCard.secondOpinionMeasuredBy: These figures were measured by the JavaScript copy of the model that actually runs in this app, not by the training framework.
modelCard.secondOpinionTradeoff: It ranks patients slightly better overall, but catches fewer diabetics than the tree. For screening that is the wrong trade, which is why it advises rather than decides.
modelCard.neuralImportanceTitle: What the neural model relies on
modelCard.neuralImportanceNote: Unlike the tree, this model gives every reading a weight, including the ones the tree never checks. The two lists are measured differently and are not directly comparable.
